notes: Static fields (url, license, preprocessing, output_semantics, engine_build) are hand-authored and are the source of truth for scripts/fetch_models.sh and scripts/build_engines.py.
Dynamic fields (onnx_sha256, onnx_bytes, engine_sha256, engine_bytes, bindings, build_latency, verify) are written by scripts/build_engines.py after a real build on this board.
Latencies are GPU compute time in milliseconds measured by trtexec on this exact board at MODE_20W_6CORE. They exclude H2D/D2H copies and all CPU pre/post-processing.
Binary .onnx and .engine files are gitignored. Reproduce with scripts/fetch_models.sh then scripts/build_engines.py.

yolov5n.license_note: Ultralytics YOLOv5 v7.0 weights are AGPL-3.0. ADAS declares MIT in pyproject.toml, so shipping or network-serving this engine is a licence conflict. Use yolox_nano / yolox_tiny (Apache-2.0) for any distributed build; yolov5n is retained only as a development baseline.

output_semantics.output0: (1, 25200, 85) float16. Per anchor: [cx, cy, w, h, objectness, 80 COCO class scores]. cx/cy/w/h are pixels in the 640x640 letterboxed frame; objectness and class scores are already sigmoid-activated. Final score = objectness * class_score. Decode in adas.perception.yolo.decode_yolo.

yolov5n.io_dtype_note: This engine binds images and output0 as HALF (float16), unlike every other engine here, which binds FLOAT. TensorRT chose the IO format when the plan was built. adas.infer.trt_engine.TrtEngine casts on the way in and out, so callers can keep passing float32, but anything that reads the raw host buffer must expect float16.

yolox_nano.license_note: Licence-clean replacement for the AGPL yolov5n. Megvii YOLOX, release 0.1.1rc0.

preprocessing.scale: none - raw 0..255 pixel values, NOT divided by 255
preprocessing.note: YOLOX's exported ONNX bakes no normalisation. yolox/data/data_augment.py::preproc pastes the aspect-preserving resize at the TOP-LEFT of a 114-filled canvas and keeps 0..255 BGR. Dividing by 255 or converting to RGB will silently destroy accuracy.
preprocessing.verified_empirically: Verified on this board against frame 150 of Ultra-Fast-Lane-Detection-v2/example.mp4 (1280x720 dashcam), counting decoded detections above 0.30 confidence: BGR + raw 0..255 gave 10 (max conf 0.640), RGB + raw gave 9 (0.600), and BOTH /255 variants gave 0 detections. Dividing by 255 does not degrade this model, it silences it completely.

output_semantics.output: (1, 3549, 85) float32 for the 416x416 model (3549 = 52^2 + 26^2 + 13^2 anchor points at strides 8/16/32). Per anchor: [x_offset, y_offset, log_w, log_h, objectness, 80 COCO class scores]. objectness/class are sigmoid-activated; the box is NOT decoded. Decode as: x = (x_offset + grid_x) * stride, y = (y_offset + grid_y) * stride, w = exp(log_w) * stride, h = exp(log_h) * stride, giving cx/cy/w/h in the 416x416 letterboxed frame. Then divide by the letterbox scale (no pad subtraction: padding is bottom/right only).
output_semantics.decode_verified: The grid+stride decode described above was run end to end on a real frame and produced correctly placed car/truck boxes, so the formula is confirmed, not inferred.

yolox_tiny.license_note: Higher-accuracy Apache-2.0 detector; same pre/post-processing as yolox_nano.

preprocessing.scale: none - raw 0..255 pixel values, NOT divided by 255
preprocessing.verified_empirically: Verified on this board against frame 150 of Ultra-Fast-Lane-Detection-v2/example.mp4 (1280x720 dashcam), counting decoded detections above 0.30 confidence: BGR + raw 0..255 gave 10 (max conf 0.640), RGB + raw gave 9 (0.600), and BOTH /255 variants gave 0 detections. Dividing by 255 does not degrade this model, it silences it completely.

output_semantics.output: Identical layout to yolox_nano: (1, 3549, 85), undecoded grid/stride offsets.
output_semantics.decode_verified: The grid+stride decode described above was run end to end on a real frame and produced correctly placed car/truck boxes, so the formula is confirmed, not inferred.

yolop.license_note: hustvl/YOLOP, MIT. Trained on BDD100K; BDD100K's own dataset terms are non-commercial, which constrains redistribution of the weights but not the MIT code.

preprocessing.note: ImageNet normalisation IS required, unlike YOLOv5.

output_semantics.det_out: (1, 25200, 6) float32 detections: [cx, cy, w, h, objectness, car_score] in the 640x640 letterboxed frame. Single class (BDD100K vehicle). Objectness and class score are sigmoid-activated and the boxes are already decoded to pixels. Needs confidence filtering and NMS.
output_semantics.drive_area_seg: (1, 2, 640, 640) float32 logits over {not-drivable, drivable}. argmax along axis 1 gives the drivable-area mask in the letterboxed frame; un-letterbox before use.
output_semantics.lane_line_seg: (1, 2, 640, 640) float32 logits over {not-lane, lane}. argmax along axis 1 gives a binary lane-line mask in the letterboxed frame.

yolop.scheduling_note: Heavier than yolov5n. Intended for a lower-rate cross-check / free-space channel, not the 20 Hz detection path. Measured GPU compute time is recorded under build_latency.

midas_v21_small.license_note: Intel ISL MiDaS v2.1 small, MIT.

preprocessing.note: Aspect ratio is NOT preserved: the frame is stretched to 256x256. Depth is scale-invariant so the distortion is tolerable, but the same stretch must be applied when sampling the map at a detection box.

output_semantics.797: (1, 256, 256) float32 INVERSE relative depth (disparity-like), unitless, with an unknown per-frame affine scale and shift. Larger value = closer. It is NOT metres and MUST NOT be published as a metric range without a per-frame least-squares alignment against a metric reference; on its own it is only an ordering / consistency channel. Bilinearly upsample to frame size before sampling.
output_semantics.binding_name_warning: The input binding is literally named "0" and the output binding "797" - the MiDaS v2.1 ONNX export kept torch's numeric tensor ids. Address them by those exact strings, or take TrtEngine.input_name / TrtEngine.output_names[0].

midas_v21_small.scheduling_note: Independent of the pinhole box-height range estimator, so it breaks that common-mode failure. Sample the median inverse depth over the lower-central region of a detection box.

ufldv2_culane_res18.license_note: Ultra-Fast-Lane-Detection-v2 (cfzd), MIT. ONNX mirrored by PINTO0309/PINTO_model_zoo entry 324 (also MIT). Trained on CULane, whose dataset terms are research-only.
ufldv2_culane_res18.size_note: The ONNX is 825 MB because UFLDv2's classification head is a single dense layer of ~186 M parameters (2048 -> (200*72 + 100*81 + 2*72 + 2*81) * 4 lanes). The FP16 engine is roughly half that on disk and must be resident in GPU memory at run time; budget for it on a 6.7 GiB board.

preprocessing.note: Canonical UFLDv2 test transform (data/dataloader.py::get_test_loader and demo.py): stretch the WHOLE frame to height int(train_height / crop_ratio) = int(320 / 0.6) = 533 and width 1600 (aspect ratio not preserved), convert to RGB, divide by 255, apply ImageNet mean/std, THEN keep the BOTTOM 320 rows (img[:, -320:, :]). The 213 cropped rows are sky. deploy/trt_infer.py in the vendored tree uses a different, demo-only crop and no mean/std - do not copy it.

output_semantics.loc_row: (1, 200, 72, 4) float32 logits: per row-anchor (72) and lane (4), a distribution over 200 horizontal cells. Expected cell = softmax over a window around argmax, weighted by cell index, + 0.5; x_crop = cell / (200 - 1) * 1600.
output_semantics.loc_col: (1, 100, 81, 4) float32 logits: per column-anchor (81) and lane (4), a distribution over 100 vertical cells. y_crop = cell / (100 - 1) * 320.
output_semantics.exist_row: (1, 2, 72, 4) float32 logits over {absent, present} per row-anchor and lane. argmax along axis 1; a row lane is used when its present-count > 72/2.
output_semantics.exist_col: (1, 2, 81, 4) float32 logits over {absent, present} per column-anchor and lane. argmax along axis 1; a column lane is used when its present-count > 81/4.
output_semantics.lane_index_convention: Lanes 1 and 2 are the ego-lane left and right markings and are decoded from the ROW heads. Lanes 0 and 3 are the adjacent-lane markings and are decoded from the COLUMN heads.
output_semantics.coordinate_frame: Decoded points are in the 1600x320 CROPPED network frame. Map back with orig_y = (y_crop + 213) / (533 / frame_height) and orig_x = x_crop / (1600 / frame_width) - note the x and y scales differ because the resize is a stretch, not a letterbox.
